adjudicated.jp: 「青春群像グラフティー」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Vitelloni Graffitea."
comments: 青春群像 is a word meaning just that, but oddly enough, it's also the Japanese title of a seminal 1950s Fellini movie http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Vitelloni I suspect this may be a reference to that and not just the word because of the second part; that's a not-uncommon transliteration for Graffiti, which, regardless of movies, with the first word suggests American Graffiti. Which was set just a few years later than Vitelloni, though it's newer by two decades, so the two fit the tone. Plus the odd tweak at the end to make a flavor of tea, in both languages, there it is. Well, that, or I dunno at all. Oh, and it means what goes on in CCA0030, especially. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Vitelloni attempts an ensemble-youth allusion and Graffitea preserves the following tea bridge. The defect is that the replacement is needlessly obscure and fails to communicate the source label to an English reader.
adjudicated.remedy: Use an intelligible youth-ensemble phrase that still supports the tea sound joke.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "D-dummy, my heart of hearts is crying, baka! Wailing, baka! This is the utsuge route!"
comments: Tsundere Mode! Girly, for starters, which needs much broader strokes in English. Baka works well for strawman tsundere (is that a term well it is now). That last one is "weeping emotional route", which is, well. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The crying, sobbing, and tearjerker progression is present. The confirmed defects are the two inserted baka interjections and the untranslated, unexplained utsuge label.
adjudicated.remedy: Preserve the escalation in fully intelligible English without inserted Japanese garnish.

highlights.text: Taichi: "D-dummy, my heart of hearts is crying, baka! Wailing, baka! This is the utsuge route!"

adjudicated.jp: 「そうは見えない～」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "None of that I can seee～."
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source’s propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 「男同士でジメジメしたって寒いだけだ、そーいうイベントは貴様のねーちゃんと起こすわい」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "But it's corny to get all tearful with males! Go trigger that event with your nee-chan, you bastard!"
comments: Curiously, this sentence ends with 'wai', which Secret Information (dictionary) reports as 'mainly male, signifying emotion'. I guess the point is the vaguely contradictory nature? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator says he will trigger that sentimental event with Tomoki’s sister instead. “Go trigger that event” orders Tomoki to do it, reversing the agent.
adjudicated.remedy: Use “I’ll save that kind of event for your sister.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "But it's corny to get all tearful with males! Go trigger that event with your nee-chan, you bastard!"

adjudicated.jp: 「ひでー！」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "Nastyyy!"
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source’s propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 「さあ、そうと決まったらとっとと働け！　放送予定日は明日じゃい」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Well, if that's your decision then get to work you whelp! Broadcast is scheduled for tomorrow ya know."
comments: Half-mirroring above -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Work, tomorrow, and the settled plan remain recoverable. If that's your decision weakens the already-settled force and assigns the decision to the addressee.
adjudicated.remedy: Use Now that that's settled before the command.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Well, if that's your decision then get to work you whelp! Broadcast is scheduled for tomorrow ya know."

adjudicated.jp: 「へいへい」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "Yeah, yeah."
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source’s propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 「じゃ機材、調達してくる」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "Well, I'll go bring up the equipment."
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source’s propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "...Taichi?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source’s propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 校舎に戻る足を止め、友貴。
adjudicated.en: A leg inside the school building, Tomoki stops.
adjudicated.assessment: The source says Tomoki stops on his way back into the school building. “A leg inside the school building” places part of him inside already and does not form a grammatical sentence.
adjudicated.remedy: Use “Tomoki stopped on his way back into the school.”

highlights.text: A leg inside the school building, Tomoki stops.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Hm?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source’s propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 「……てっきり姉貴と仲直りしろとか言うのかなって思ってた、姉貴を手伝えよ弟だろって」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "...I thought you would tell me to put things right with Aneki, for sure, that a younger brother should help his Aneki."
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source’s propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 「いや、姉弟喧嘩なんてごくまっとうな人生じゃん。止めんよ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Naaah, sibling quarreling's a very respectable way of life it is. Don'tcha stop."
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator says sibling quarrels are normal and that he will not stop theirs. “Don’tcha stop” tells Tomoki not to stop, changing the speaker’s policy into a command.
adjudicated.remedy: Use “Sibling quarrels are perfectly normal. I’m not going to interfere.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Naaah, sibling quarreling's a very respectable way of life it is. Don'tcha stop."

adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source’s propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 「要するに俺様を手伝えということだ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Basically this is about you helping the greatness that is I."
adjudicated.assessment: “The greatness that is I” uses the wrong pronoun case and awkwardly expands 俺様.
adjudicated.remedy: Use “In short, you’re here to help the great me.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Basically this is about you helping the greatness that is I."

adjudicated.jp: 胸を張る。
adjudicated.en: Puff that chest with pride!
adjudicated.assessment: The source narrates that he puffs out his chest. “Puff that chest with pride!” changes narration into a command addressed to someone else.
adjudicated.remedy: Use “I puffed out my chest.”

highlights.text: Puff that chest with pride!

adjudicated.jp: 「……おまえ大物」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "...what're you a VIP."
adjudicated.assessment: VIP can gesture toward big-shot status, but the malformed question changes the compact statement into a less precise incredulous status query.
adjudicated.remedy: Use a grammatical statement such as You're a real piece of work.

highlights.text: Tomoki: "...what're you a VIP."

adjudicated.jp: 「適応係数８０オーバーのオーバーロードですから」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "After all, I am the Overlord of all those of Conformity Coefficient 80 and Over."
comments: 8 and 0, the Error and the loop. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source says he is an Overlord with an adaptation coefficient above eighty. The English makes him ruler “of all those” above eighty, adding a hierarchy and other people.
adjudicated.remedy: Use “I’m an Overlord with an adaptation coefficient over eighty.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "After all, I am the Overlord of all those of Conformity Coefficient 80 and Over."

adjudicated.jp: 「……そのオーバーロードとも、これからも普通に友達してやるよ」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "...and I will still be this Overlord's normal friend from now on."
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source’s propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 「そういうの、嫌いじゃないから」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "Because... I don't hate that of you."
comments: See CCA0007. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The favorable attitude survives. That of you is ungrammatical and narrows the behavior into an awkward possessed trait.
adjudicated.remedy: Use I don't dislike that about you.

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Because... I don't hate that of you."

adjudicated.jp: さっと校舎内に消えた。逃げるように。
adjudicated.en: He quickly vanishes inside the school building. As if running away.
adjudicated.assessment: The past narration says he quickly disappeared into the building. “Vanishes” shifts into present tense.
adjudicated.remedy: Use “He quickly disappeared into the school building, as if fleeing.”

highlights.text: He quickly vanishes inside the school building. As if running away.

adjudicated.jp: 「キライジャナイカラ……ププ！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "'Iiii don't haaate that of youuu'... pffft!"
comments: Ridiculing. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source’s propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: そう言った友貴は、一瞬で人類の限界まで赤面しきっていた。
adjudicated.en: After Tomoki had said that, his face had instantly reddened up to the physical blushing limits of mankind.
comments: awww they do love each o--wait waIT WAAAAAIT -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source says Tomoki flushed to the human limit in an instant. The pluperfect “had instantly reddened up” is unnecessarily tangled and misaligned with the simple past sequence.
adjudicated.remedy: Use “Tomoki instantly flushed as red as humanly possible.”

highlights.text: After Tomoki had said that, his face had instantly reddened up to the physical blushing limits of mankind.

adjudicated.remedy: Use “I am fighting.”
